title: Vendor llama.cpp at b10180
description: Clone llama.cpp (b10180) into third_party/llama.cpp/ as a vendored tree. Keep it as a regular directory under our control so we can patch it.

title: Patch llama.cpp with per-tensor data callback
description: Identify the right hook point: somewhere in llama_model_loader.cpp / tensor loading code, add a per-shard `tensor_data_callback` to llama_model_params that, given a tensor name + byte range, mmaps the corresponding shard and returns a pointer. Original behavior: a single mmap of the whole file. New behavior: lazy per-tensor mmap with the address belonging to the lifetime of a single tensor load, then immediate munmap.

title: Build the loader manifest
description: Add a small sharder manifest that tells our patched loader how to map each tensor name to a shard file + offset. The sharder already writes this (blk.N.meta.json) but for the loader we need a different layout: given a tensor name like 'blk.0.ssm_in.weight', look up which shard + offset.

title: Wire patched llama.cpp into Remora
description: After patching, build the patched llama.cpp as a static library and link our existing remora_core against it. The driver (our new main) initializes the patched loader, runs llama_decode per token, prints results.

title: Run real benchmark
description: Run scripts/bench_compare.sh. Remora now produces real text. Confirm peak RSS is meaningfully lower than llama-cli (loaded monolithically). Compare TTFT and TPS.
